key_insight: Physics-localized hyper-reduction preserves coupled elastoplastic soil deformation and water-flow predictions while delivering up to 77× speed-up.
engineering_relevance: Faster repeated dam simulations can support calibration, uncertainty quantification and safety scenario analysis.
method: Build separate POD reduced bases for displacement and pore pressure.
Compute affine residual terms exactly and approximate nonlinear corrections with separate ECSW cubature rules for each balance equation.
Assemble original FEniCSx variational forms only on selected elements concentrated in plastified and unsaturated zones.
evidence_signal: Tests on 2D and 3D dams under raising and consolidation, with material properties and raise height varied, reported displacement and pressure errors below 0.5% relative to finite element solutions and speed-ups up to 43× and 77×, respectively.
watch_item: Accuracy beyond the tested parameter ranges and loading scenarios remains to be established.
paper_title: A hyper-reduction strategy for elastoplastic hydro-mechanical problems in partially saturated soil
